agentCan: Implement the full authorization-code flow and per-user token storage
Handle disconnects (delete stored token and sync config, per the docs' explicit obligation)
Rotate the client secret and update configuration

approval.trigger: No review is required before real users can connect; no approval step, queue, or user cap exists for connections. The only review-like gate is the optional Mailchimp Integration Partner Program, which controls a Marketplace LISTING, not connections, and requires your integration to already have 25+ active users within the past 90 days.
approval.wait: None for connections; partner-program review duration is not published

blockers.detail: The authorize request has no scope parameter and the docs describe no granular permissions: authorization is all-or-nothing at whatever the authorizing user can access. There is no least-privilege strategy to apply, and your security review story must acknowledge that.
blockers.howToClear: You cannot clear it; design for it. Request the connection only when you need it, and be transparent with users about the breadth.
blockers.title: No scopes: all-or-nothing authorization

blockers.detail: The client_secret is shown only once at registration. Lose it and the recovery path is rotation, after which requests signed with the old secret fail with a 401.
blockers.howToClear: Vault the secret at registration; use the documented rotation flow if it is ever exposed.
blockers.title: Client secret shown exactly once

tested: Read-only verification: registration model, flow endpoints, token behavior, and the partner-program listing gate were checked against current mailchimp.com/developer pages (no app registered, nothing submitted)

Any per-user data-center routing or metadata endpoint after token exchange (third-party docs describe one; current official pages read do not mention it).
Partner-program review timeline and listing criteria beyond the application form; any fees beyond the 'free to apply' statement.

flavor.recommended: A registered application in your Mailchimp account: OAuth 2 authorization code against the Marketing API
flavor.why: There is effectively one flavor. The docs describe OAuth 2 as how third-party integrations work (Zapier, Slack, Shopify authenticate this way) and as a requirement for a Marketplace listing. Users authorize on Mailchimp's page; you store one access token per user.

humanMust: Register the application in your own Mailchimp account and vault the client secret (shown once)
Apply to the partner program if you want a Marketplace listing (after reaching 25+ active users)
name: Mailchimp
nuances: Tokens never expire, so there is no refresh token and nothing to rotate on a schedule; a token dies only on user revocation or user removal from the account.
A token that stops working means the user revoked you; the docs say retrying won't help, send them back through the authorization flow.
HTTPS for the redirect URI is strongly recommended but, unusually, not enforced.
OAuth here covers the Marketing API; no OAuth path for other Mailchimp APIs is described.
The partner program's 25+ active users prerequisite means a new app cannot be listed at launch even if it wants the review; listing is deliberately post-traction.
prerequisites: Secure storage for the client secret and per-user access tokens

steps.detail: Register the application in your Mailchimp account; copy the client_id (public identifier) and client_secret (shown only once; rotatable if exposed).
steps.title: Register the application

steps.detail: Set the URL Mailchimp returns users to after authorization. All OAuth endpoint traffic is HTTPS; HTTPS for the redirect URI itself is strongly recommended but not enforced.
steps.title: Configure the redirect URI

steps.detail: Send the user to login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri. The user logs in and authorizes on Mailchimp's page. There is no scope parameter to set.
steps.title: Redirect the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST to login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, and the code. The secret never touches the browser.
steps.title: Exchange the code for a token

steps.detail: Persist one access token per user and call the Marketing API with it. Tokens have no expiry and there is no refresh token. On disconnect/uninstall, delete the stored token and any syncing configuration (an explicit documented obligation).
steps.title: Store the token and call the API

tagline: One of the simplest OAuth programs in this library: register an app, run a standard code flow, done. Two quirks define it: there are no scopes at all, and tokens never expire.

time.active: ~10 min of registration plus a standard authorization-code implementation
time.total: Same day; no review stands between registration and real users
